issues.description: The problem statement's Part 2 text requires a method signature messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) (including a double parameter and a return format containing the volume), but the UML in the same problem statement and the provided solution implement messageOnMilk() with no parameters. This mismatch between the textual requirement and the UML/solution will confuse students about which signature to implement and which behavior/tests to satisfy.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the conflicting specification. Either (A) update the problem statement text in Part 2 to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and adjust the example return format to match the UML and solution (e.g. "[Animal Type] [name] is milked"), or (B) change the UML and the solution to define messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update all implementations and tests to accept the double parameter and include the volume in the returned string. Prefer updating the problem statement to match the existing UML and solution (option A) if tests expect the no-parameter version.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a method messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) (with a double parameter and a specific return format including the volume), but the UML, template usage, and the solution define messageOnMilk() with no parameters. This signature mismatch (same conceptual method with different parameterization) creates confusion about the required method signature, return format, and how to call it, and can lead students to implement the wrong API or face compilation/test mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Update the problem statement to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and a simple return like "[Animal Type] [name] is milked" (aligning with UML, template usage, and solution), or (B) update the interface, all implementing classes, and all call sites (including Main and UML) to use messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and return the specified string including the volume. Ensure the UML, template code, and examples in the problem text all reflect the chosen signature.
